draft.title: Determinants and area
card: For the matrix [a b; c d], the determinant is det = ad − bc.
A transformation scales every area by the absolute value of the determinant. New area = |det| × old area.
If det is negative, the shape is flipped over (its orientation reverses), but the area still scales by |det|. If det = 0, the plane collapses onto a line or point.
Example: [3 1; 2 2] has det = 3×2 − 1×2 = 4. A triangle of area 5 becomes a triangle of area 20. Rotations and reflections have |det| = 1, so they keep areas and lengths the same.
draft.remember: Areas scale by |ad − bc|. A negative determinant flips the shape but does not shrink area.

a.q: A matrix [4 1; 2 3] is applied to a shape of area 6. What is the area of the image?
a.why: det = 4×3 − 1×2 = 10, so the area is 10 × 6 = 60. Using 4×3 alone, or adding instead of subtracting, gives a different scale factor that is wrong.
a.clue: Work out ad − bc first, then multiply by the old area.

b.q: The matrix [1 2; 3 1] is applied to a square of area 4. What is the area of the image, and what happens to its orientation?
b.why: det = 1×1 − 2×3 = −5. Area scales by |−5| = 5, so the new area is 20. The negative sign means the orientation is reversed, but an area is never negative.
b.clue: Area uses the absolute value, but the sign still tells you about flipping.

problems.detail: 'A negative determinant flips the shape but does not shrink area' is false as a general statement. A determinant such as −0.5 flips the shape and halves its area. The card only says the area scales by |det|. The line means the sign does not shrink the area, but students will read it as negative determinants never shrinking area.

'Rotations and reflections have |det| = 1, so they keep areas and lengths the same' implies that |det| = 1 is why lengths are kept. It is not: a shear such as [1 1; 0 1] has det = 1 but changes lengths. |det| = 1 only guarantees that area is kept.

check.summary: Both questions are correct (60; 20 and flipped). The remember line wrongly suggests a negative determinant never shrinks area, and the card implies |det| = 1 keeps lengths, which shears disprove.
